A01.notes: Edits routed through execCommand('insertText') to stay on native textarea undo; no JS undo stack. 'notes will be lost when the tab closes' banner only on localStorage unavailable = failure state.

A02.notes: Ctrl+S bound to downloadNote(), not a storage commit, so no user-invoked in-browser save. Genuine undo stack: 200 snapshots, 600ms coalescing, per-note timeline.

A03.notes: No undo/redo at all; no Ctrl+Z handler, programmatic edits assign textarea.value directly, destroying native undo. Import is file-picker only. Storage warning is a failure state.

A04.notes: Ctrl+S genuinely commits to localStorage (saveNow->storage.save). Real snapshot undo stack via core.createHistory. A comment says the mobile drawer state is deliberately not saved, but that is layout, not document content.

A05.notes: Ctrl+S bound to downloadNote(); persistNow only on window.Notepad, so no user-invoked storage commit. Genuine per-note snapshot history with coalescing. 'Not saved' and private-browsing warning are failure states.

A06.notes: No JS undo; applyEdit pushes through execCommand('insertText'/'delete') to keep native undo. Save button and Ctrl+S write a .txt rather than committing to storage. Blocked-storage banner is a failure state.

A07.notes: applyEdit uses execCommand('insertText') with a comment saying it is the only way to keep native undo alive; no JS history. Storage-failure banner is a failure state.

A08.notes: Genuine JS undo/redo per note, 200 entries, 700ms coalescing. Ctrl+S downloads .txt; no on-demand localStorage commit (flushSave internal only). One dead 'unsaved' label string.

A09.notes: No JS undo stack; applyEdit routes changes through execCommand('insertText') to keep native undo. Blocked-storage warning and 'Saving is off' badge are failure states.

A10.notes: Ctrl+Z/Y in shortcuts dialog but no JS implements them; native textarea undo preserved via execCommand('insertText'). Only JS undo is delete-restore toast. Storage-blocked banner is a failure state.

A11.notes: setEditorText computes minimal diff and uses execCommand('insertText') specifically to preserve native undo (comment says so); no JS undo/redo. Storage warning fires only when localStorage unavailable.

A12.notes: undoRemove is single-slot for note deletion only; no text undo/redo stack, no Ctrl+Z binding, replace/import assign textarea.value discarding native stack. Ephemeral strings limited to blocked-storage failure label.

A13.notes: Real JS snapshot timeline per note (createHistory, 200 steps, coalescing). Ctrl+S saves .txt to disk, not storage; flush() only via window.NotepadApp test API. Blocked-storage label is a failure state.

A14.notes: Custom per-note undo stack (250 steps, diff coalescing) on Ctrl+Z/Y. Ctrl+S exports .txt; saveNow() only on window.Notepad with nothing bound to it. Private-mode toast is a blocked-storage warning.

A15.notes: No JS undo at all; nothing binds Ctrl+Z, and Tab-indent plus find/replace assign textarea.value directly, wiping even native undo. Ctrl+S genuinely calls store.flush()->setItem.

A16.notes: JS undo/redo snapshot timeline, 300 steps, typing-run coalescing. Ctrl+S wired to downloadActive (disk), so no user-invoked storage commit. Blocked-storage banner is a failure-state warning.

A17.notes: Per-note JS History class with tag-based coalescing. No user-invoked storage save. On corrupt payload writes a notepad.backup.<ts> key that no code reads back (write-only dead data).

A18.notes: Real explicit save: file.save 'Save now' Ctrl+S calls flushSave->store.persist; disk export moved to Ctrl+Shift+S. Per-note JS undo stack, 300 entries, word-level coalescing.

A19.notes: Real per-note snapshot array (NotepadCore.history) wired to Mod+Z/Mod+Shift+Z. Ctrl+S bound to 'Save a copy to a file'. Has split markdown preview. 'Changes are not saved' only when storage blocked.

A20.notes: Explicit save exists only as the Ctrl+S shortcut (ACTIONS['save-now']->saveNow()); no button or menu item carries it, though the shortcuts dialog documents it. JS snapshot stack with typing coalescing.

A21.notes: No text undo/redo at all; no history stack, no Ctrl+Z binding, and setBody()/Tab-indent assign editor.value directly, destroying native undo too. Trash is a deleted-items list, not an access history.

A22.notes: Genuine JS snapshot stack per note (core.createHistory, 250 entries); beforeinput intercepts historyUndo/historyRedo so native undo routes into it. Ctrl+S is a .txt export. Ephemeral wording only when localStorage blocked.

A23.notes: Ctrl+S is a real 'Save now' calling flushSave(). No JS undo stack; a code comment states execCommand('insertText') is used precisely to preserve native textarea undo. 'Notes will not be kept' toast only when storage blocked.

A24.notes: Ctrl+S labelled 'Download as .txt'; it calls flushSave() first so storage is incidentally committed, but there is no user-facing save-to-storage command. Undo deliberately left to browser via minimal-span execCommand.

A25.notes: Ctrl+Z/Y in shortcuts dialog but no JS handler; native undo preserved via execCommand('insertText') with value-assignment fallback. 'Changes are not being saved' banner is a blocked/full-storage failure warning.

A26.notes: No JS undo stack and no undo shortcut bound; commitBody assigns textarea.value directly, discarding native history for programmatic edits. Open-from-disk limited to .json backups via picker, no plain-text open or drag-drop.

A27.notes: Shortcuts modal labels Ctrl+Z/Y as 'your browser's own'; applyText diffs and uses execCommand('insertText') to keep native history. Only JS undo actions are one-shot toasts for delete and replace-all.

A28.notes: Genuine per-note snapshot stack in NotepadCore.history, 200 entries, time-coalesced. Ctrl+S downloads .txt; storage writes purely automatic. storage.upgrade() is an intentional no-op migration hook.

A29.notes: Shortcut table lists Ctrl+Z/Y but no JS handler exists; JS undoStack is only for restoring deleted notes. 'Notes will be lost when the tab closes' is a blocked-storage failure state.

A30.notes: Help panel says 'Undo / redo (your browser's own editor history)'; insertText uses execCommand to preserve it. JS pushUndo is a single whole-document snapshot for destructive actions, not an editor undo stack.
